original_abstract.text: Sparse computation can scale the parametric capacity of LLMs without proportionally increasing active computation, but pretraining sparse architectures remains expensive and data-hungry. Existing sparse upcycling methods mainly target Mixture-of-Experts models, where expert homogeneity, sample inefficiency, and system overheads can limit practical scalability. Static sparse memory offers predictable access and token-specific updates that can help address these challenges, but naively integrating it into pretrained computation yields poor returns. In this work, we introduce STAPLE, a recipe built upon STEM for integrating static sparse memory into pretrained models. Whereas STEM replaces FFN up-projections with token-indexed embeddings, STAPLE retains them and adds the embeddings as a residual pathway, preserving pretrained computation while learning complementary token-specific information in a scalable manner. On OLMo-2 1B, STAPLE improves over continued dense training by 4.27 points on HumanEval, 2.80 on MBPP, 2.27 on GSM8K, and 1.65 on DROP. Average performance increases with static capacity, and improvements persist on the larger OLMo-2 7B backbone. STAPLE also outperforms static sparse baselines such as STEM and an Engram-style model, and achieves a higher average score than an MoE upcycling baseline while decoding 2x faster with less than half its GPU model memory and measured GPU energy per token in our throughput-oriented decoding evaluation. Importantly, despite introducing billions of parameters late in training, our host-offloaded implementation keeps generation throughput within 1.5% and training throughput within 3% of the dense baseline, while caching only the ~5% most frequent embeddings on GPU. These results show that static sparse memory can provide a sample-efficient, scalable, and sustainable path for expanding pretrained models without sparse pretraining from scratch.
original_abstract.source_title: STAPLE: Static Sparse Upcycling of Pretrained Checkpoints via Embedding Modules

en.text: STAPLE adds token-indexed embedding memory as a residual path while retaining pretrained feed-forward computation, expanding sparse capacity without starting pretraining over. OLMo-2 1B and 7B experiments support gains over continued dense training. In its throughput-oriented setup, host offloading and caching roughly the most frequent 5% of embeddings keep generation throughput within 1.5% of the dense baseline. Token-specific memory offers a possible recommendation-scaling design; host memory and transfer costs remain, and no CTR gains are established.

zh.text: STAPLE 保留预训练前馈网络，把按token索引的Embedding记忆作为残差支路接入，扩充稀疏容量，无需从头预训练。OLMo-2 1B和7B实验显示相对继续训练稠密模型的收益；在所测吞吐配置中，主机卸载并缓存约5%最高频Embedding后，生成吞吐与稠密基线差距在1.5%以内。可借鉴这种增量扩容方式，但仍有主机内存与传输成本，未验证CTR收益。

original_abstract.text: Efficient autoregressive generation is increasingly limited by the memory footprint of the key-value (KV) cache, which grows linearly with sequence length, batch size, and model depth. Existing approaches such as Multi-Query Attention (MQA), Grouped-Query Attention (GQA), Multi-Head Latent Attention (MLA), and Tensor Product Attention (TPA) reduce this cost through different trade-offs, but often sacrifice expressivity, require additional positional-encoding machinery, or impose restrictive low-rank structure. We propose Kronecker Product Attention (KPA), which represents key and value activations as sums of Kronecker products of compact, token-dependent matrix factors. KPA strictly generalizes TPA: rank-one vector-outer-product factorization arises as a degenerate Kronecker split, while non-degenerate matrix factors can represent richer block-structured patterns. We further show that a structured rotary embedding operator matched to the Kronecker representation preserves the relative-position property of RoPE while rotating only the compact factors, removing the need for a decoupled RoPE branch as in MLA. Empirically, KPA matches or exceeds TPA, MHA, MQA, GQA, and MLA across four model scales and nine downstream benchmarks under identical training conditions, while achieving up to 10x KV cache compression. The Kronecker head split is a tuneable hyperparameter that allows practitioners to navigate the compression-accuracy trade-off at design time without architectural changes.
original_abstract.source_title: Kronecker Product Attention: Memory-Efficient KV Compression via Structured Factorization

en.text: KPA represents keys and values as sums of Kronecker products of compact token-dependent matrix factors and applies compatible rotary position transformations directly to those factors. Across four language-model scales and nine benchmarks, the paper reports competitive accuracy with up to 10x KV-cache compression. Its structured factorization may inform memory-efficient long-sequence recommendation architectures; these language-model results do not establish CTR improvements or equivalent end-to-end serving speedups.

zh.text: KPA 把键和值表示为多个紧凑矩阵因子的Kronecker积之和，并直接在因子上施加相容的位置旋转。论文在四种语言模型规模、九项基准上报告有竞争力的精度，KV缓存最多压缩10倍。可借鉴其长序列记忆的结构化分解，但语言模型结果不能直接视为CTR提升，也不等于端到端服务加速10倍。

original_abstract.text: RDMA can reduce communication overhead in distributed machine learning systems, but realizing these benefits in production requires more than replacing TCP. Variable-size messages, concurrent connections, bursty incasts, and service failures introduce challenges that hardware offload alone cannot address. This paper reports our experience deploying ByteExpress, a software communication layer over hardware RDMA, in ByteDance's parameter-server-based inference and training systems. We present three lessons from the deployment: efficient RDMA requires buffer management across application and transport layers; scalable communication requires coordinated management of connections, receive capacity, and outstanding data; and service availability requires recovery above the transport layer. ByteExpress combines an RDMA-aware allocator, zero-copy transfers, QP multiplexing, receive-credit flow control, a software send window, and RPC-assisted recovery. In production inference, ByteExpress reduces mean and P99 model parameter fetch latency by 35.7% and 43.7%, respectively, and total CPU usage by 10.69% compared with kernel TCP. In training, ByteExpress reduces P99 model parameter push latency by up to 74.0% compared with TCP, with no PFC pauses observed at runtime.
original_abstract.source_title: Deploying RDMA for Distributed Inference and Training At Scale

en.text: ByteExpress is a software communication layer for RDMA in ByteDance parameter-server-based inference and training. It combines buffer management, zero-copy transfers, connection multiplexing, flow control, and recovery above the transport layer. Production inference reports 35.7% lower mean and 43.7% lower P99 parameter-fetch latency, plus 10.69% lower total CPU use versus kernel TCP. It directly informs recommendation parameter-serving infrastructure; these are communication and system metrics, not ranking-quality gains.

zh.text: ByteExpress 面向字节跳动参数服务器式训练与推理，结合缓冲区管理、零拷贝、连接复用、流控和传输层之上的故障恢复。生产推理中，相对内核 TCP，参数获取平均延迟降低35.7%、P99延迟降低43.7%，总CPU用量降低10.69%。可直接参考其推荐参数服务设计；这些是通信与系统指标，不是排序质量收益。

original_abstract.text: Generative recommendation (GR) of social media platforms commonly retrieves items by autoregressively decoding discrete Semantic IDs (SIDs) with finite-width beam search. This work examines how this output interface constrains whether held-out targets enter finite returned lists, while distinguishing catalog-wide scoreability from empirical top-K support. We introduce two continuous-query paradigms: CQG-Single generates one retrieval query in a single pass, and CQG-AR autoregressively generates continuous residual updates, retaining step-wise decoding while removing the SID item-token vocabulary, code lookup, and discrete beam expansion. These designs thereby eliminate the SID-specific reachability constraint induced by finite-beam decoding and avoid the technical challenge of aligning a discrete SID vocabulary with the pretrained backbone's vector space. Both methods make every encoded item directly scoreable through dense or approximate-nearest-neighbor retrieval. Under a unified protocol with valid-prefix constrained decoding, CQG-Single exceeds the TIGER-style baseline in all seven runs while using 55.3% as many trainable parameters. CQG-AR remains comparable on ML-1M and is numerically stronger on Beauty and Sports datasets. A controlled depth ablation further shows that additional continuous refinement does not monotonically improve shallow accuracy. These findings motivate decoupling output representation, autoregressive modeling, and retrieval budget when evaluating generative recommendation systems.
original_abstract.source_title: Beyond Semantic IDs: Finite-Beam Reachability and Continuous-Query Generation in Generative Recommendation

en.text: CQG replaces discrete semantic-ID beam expansion with a generated continuous retrieval query, either in one pass or through autoregressive residual refinement. On MovieLens-1M, Beauty, and Sports, it separates finite-beam target reachability from the ability to score every indexed item. CQG-Single beats the TIGER-style baseline in all seven MovieLens runs with 55.3% as many trainable parameters; stronger continuous-query expressiveness does not guarantee higher top-K recall, and full-rank SASRec remains strongest on Sports. Production latency and index-update costs are unmeasured.

zh.text: CQG 用生成的连续检索向量替代离散语义 ID 的束搜索展开，可一次生成，也可自回归累积残差。实验覆盖 MovieLens-1M、Beauty 和 Sports，区分有限候选列表能否包含目标与所有索引商品能否被打分。CQG-Single 在 MovieLens 的 7 次运行中均超过 TIGER 风格基线，可训练参数为其 55.3%；可打分范围扩大不保证 top-K 召回更高，Sports 上完整 SASRec 仍最强。生产延迟和索引更新成本尚未测量。

original_abstract.text: Recurrent-depth language models improve inference-time reasoning by repeatedly applying a shared network to refine internal representations, but the additional recurrent computation also increases inference cost. This overhead is particularly pronounced during long-context prefill, where the full input sequence is repeatedly processed across recurrent depth. Weight-and-activation quantization offers a natural way to accelerate this computation through lower-precision arithmetic, yet repeatedly applying quantized computation introduces numerical perturbations that accumulate along the recurrent trajectory. We systematically analyze how such errors propagate across recurrent depth and show that quantization errors introduced earlier are attenuated by more subsequent recurrent steps and therefore have a smaller effect on the final representation. Matched-budget experiments strongly support this prediction, showing that placing quantized computation earlier in recurrent depth consistently yields the best fidelity. Based on this insight, we introduce RAMP (Recurrent Adaptive Mixed Precision), which performs early recurrent refinement using low-precision weight-and-activation computation and restores high precision for terminal refinement. Across context lengths up to 4K, RAMP preserves near-full-precision prefill quality while achieving up to 1.16x end-to-end first-prefill speedup on an NVIDIA H100, corresponding to a 13.9% latency reduction.
original_abstract.source_title: RAMP: Recurrent Adaptive Mixed Precision for Efficient Prefill in Recurrent-Depth Language Models

en.text: RAMP reduces recurrent-depth prefill cost by using low-precision weights and activations in early iterations and restoring high precision for final refinement. Matched-budget experiments support greater tolerance of early quantization errors. At contexts up to 4K on an NVIDIA H100, it preserves near-full-precision prefill quality and achieves up to 1.16x end-to-end first-prefill speedup. This is a tested prefill result, with recommendation transfer unverified.

zh.text: 循环模型反复处理整段输入，预填充开销随循环增加。RAMP在早期轮次使用低精度权重和激活，在最终细化阶段恢复高精度，利用后续迭代对早期误差的缓解作用。在H100、最长4K上下文实验中，保持接近全精度的预填充质量，并实现最高1.16倍首次预填充端到端加速；推荐场景尚未验证。

original_abstract.text: In this paper, we propose Data-Adaptive Mahalanobis Cross-Head Attention (DAMCHA), a simple and effective attention mechanism that generalizes Multi-Head Attention (MHA) through the lens of metric learning. Standard MHA implicitly learns a static, head-wise Euclidean similarity corresponding to the diagonal blocks of a unified cross-head metric matrix, discarding all off-diagonal interactions across heads. DAMCHA addresses this limitation via two key innovations. First, it learns the full cross-head metric matrix, inducing a Mahalanobis-like similarity that explicitly captures inter-head interactions beyond the restricted block-diagonal structure of MHA. Second, it parameterizes the metric matrix as an input-dependent function, enabling the attention geometry to dynamically adapt to the intrinsic manifold structure of the data rather than remaining fixed after training. We further introduce principled regularization strategies, most notably stack-wise parameter sharing, to ensure computational efficiency and stable optimization. DAMCHA serves as a drop-in replacement for MHA and its variants in various Transformer architectures, delivering superior expressive power and learning performance with comparable or reduced computational overhead. Extensive experiments demonstrate that DAMCHA-based Transformers consistently outperform competing baselines across a range of benchmark tasks. Code is available at https://github.com/erwinmsmith/DAMCHA.
original_abstract.source_title: Data-Adaptive Mahalanobis Metric Learning for Cross-Head Attention in Transformers

en.text: DAMCHA extends multi-head attention with an input-dependent full cross-head metric, allowing interactions omitted by independent head-wise similarities. Stack-wise parameter sharing and regularization target stable, efficient training. The authors report improvements across evaluated Transformer tasks with comparable or reduced computational overhead. Cross-head feature interactions are a potential recommendation application, not an established result of this study.

zh.text: 多头注意力通常分别计算各头的相似性。DAMCHA引入随输入变化的跨头度量，显式建模不同头之间的交互，并用堆叠层之间的参数共享及正则化控制开销和训练稳定性。作者在所测Transformer任务上报告性能改善，计算开销相当或更低。将这种跨头交互用于推荐特征建模仍属待验证方向。

original_abstract.text: Serving a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) model pays for expert precision twice: the resident footprint pays for every expert the router can reach, while each batch-one decode step pays only for the experts it selects. These are two different rate functionals over the same per-expert widths, yet published per-expert MoE allocators constrain only the first. We call the difference the store-read gap; in the released BitsMoE checkpoint, 2.54 bits per weight (bpw) of storage become 7.50 bpw of decode traffic. We propose DuoRate, which stores once and reads per workload. Offline, it stores one uniform tier of a prefix-readable weight stream and bakes a distortion tensor. Online, it profiles a workload's own prefill without labels and solves a Lagrangian rate-distortion allocation under the decode functional; routing frequency provably cancels from every per-expert decision, and the solve costs one dot product per expert and a bisection. A deployment therefore keeps a single artifact that prefill reads at the stored rate and decode reads at the workload's own rate. On Qwen3-30B-A3B, DuoRate reading 2.3 bpw exceeds every 2-bit-class baseline by 6.3 to 47.0 points of average accuracy, and at 2.9 bpw it matches 4-bit formats that read 1.4-1.6 bpw more. The advantage is largest under long decoding: on GSM8K, DuoRate at 2.9 bpw matches or exceeds every 4-bit format and trails BF16 by only 0.25 points, and at 2.6 bpw it still matches or exceeds the 4.5-bit NF4 and FP4. Against controls in its own format, the allocation alone is worth 0.07-0.11 bpw of read rate. Code will be released upon publication.
original_abstract.source_title: DuoRate: Two-Rate Per-Expert Precision Allocation for Mixture-of-Experts Serving

en.text: DuoRate separates precision budgets for storing all MoE experts and reading selected experts during batch-one decoding. Label-free prefill profiles drive workload-specific per-expert allocation. On Qwen3-30B-A3B, quality matches evaluated 4-bit formats at a layout-derived read budget of 2.9 bits per weight. The prefix-read kernel and end-to-end traffic/latency measurements remain future work. This allocation principle may inform recommendation MoEs, but that transfer is untested; larger batches narrow the store-read distinction.

zh.text: DuoRate 分开建模全部MoE专家的存储精度预算与batch=1解码时已选专家的读取预算，用无需标签的prefill统计为各工作负载分配专家精度。在Qwen3-30B-A3B上，按存储布局计算的读取预算为2.9 bit/weight时，精度可匹配所测4位格式。前缀读取内核及端到端流量、延迟实测仍待完成。可借鉴其推荐MoE精度分配思路，但迁移尚未验证；较大batch会缩小存储与读取的差别。

original_abstract.text: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models have become the standard architecture for frontier LLMs. The multiple parallel experts in each transformer block theoretically enable expert specialization according to categories such as domains, languages, or modalities during pretraining. However, when data is imbalanced across categories, minority categories can become concentrated in a small fraction of the expert pool or spread inefficiently across them, effectively limiting their available capacity. In this work, we demonstrate that category-conditioned expert-selection biases can preferentially route tokens from different categories toward specialized expert pools. By applying biases based on input category, we provide a simple way to induce soft category-aligned specialization. This intervention encourages categories toward distinct expert subsets while retaining cross-category sharing when useful. More importantly, it enables the over-allocation of expert capacity to categories that would otherwise be disadvantaged by data scarcity. We observe performance improvements across modalities, low-resource languages, and code in models up to 10.6B parameters. At our smallest and largest model scales, these gains are equivalent to allocating 18.5% and 2.7% additional baseline training tokens, respectively. Overall, our results show that expert biases can serve as a lightweight control for category-level expert allocation, making room for low-resource categories while retaining standard MoE inference.
original_abstract.source_title: Overcoming Data Imbalances with Expert Selection Biases

en.text: Category-conditioned expert-selection biases steer low-resource categories toward dedicated expert subsets while permitting cross-category sharing. The study evaluates multimodal, multilingual, and multi-domain MoEs up to 10.6B total parameters and finds benefits for scarce categories. It suggests a controllable way to allocate sparse capacity across recommendation domains, but that transfer is untested. Training requires category labels and allocation choices; the bias can be removed at inference, avoiding inference-time category labels. Strong load-balancing regularization can suppress the effect.

zh.text: 该方法按数据类别给专家选择分数加偏置，引导低资源类别使用特定专家子集，同时保留跨类别共享。实验覆盖多模态、多语言和多领域MoE，最大总参数量10.6B，稀缺类别表现改善。它提供了按推荐领域分配稀疏容量的可借鉴控制方式，但迁移效果尚未验证；训练需要类别标签与分配方案；推理可移除偏置，无需类别标签。过强的负载均衡正则会压制效果。

original_abstract.text: Modern attention workloads require diverse masking patterns whose boundaries depend on runtime metadata, yet efficient attention kernels natively support only a small set of patterns. Existing methods for supporting custom masks in these kernels face an expressiveness-efficiency trade-off. Predicate-based methods are expressive but incur substantial preprocessing and execution overhead, whereas interval-based methods execute efficiently but restrict expressiveness through a predefined interval count. We present CompileMask, which addresses this trade-off by connecting expressive mask specifications with efficient attention execution. We design a compiler that analyzes visibility rules during the offline stage and generates a mask-specific preprocess kernel. We further propose MaskSpec, a region-based DSL that lets users express these rules. During the online stage, the generated kernel reads batch metadata and produces a compact Execution Descriptor that lets the attention kernel efficiently check visibility by comparing element indices against precomputed endpoints. Experiments show that CompileMask achieves up to $3.8\times$ speedup over state-of-the-art methods.
original_abstract.source_title: CompileMask: Bridging the Gap Between Expressiveness and Efficiency in Attention Masking

en.text: CompileMask compiles region-based visibility rules into metadata-driven preprocessing kernels and compact endpoint descriptors, reducing custom attention-mask overhead. It tests HSTU, shared-prompt, local multimodal, and causal patterns on Blackwell GPUs. Qwen3-8B training with packed KuaiRand length traces and HSTU masks reaches 1.33× the throughput of FlexAttention with the FA4 backend. This directly informs custom-mask implementation for recommendation, but does not measure recommendation accuracy gains.

zh.text: CompileMask 将区域式可见性规则编译成读取批次元数据的预处理核和紧凑端点描述，降低自定义注意力掩码开销。论文在 Blackwell GPU 上测试 HSTU、共享提示、多模态局部与因果模式；采用 KuaiRand 序列长度、打包输入和 HSTU 掩码的 Qwen3-8B 训练，吞吐为 FlexAttention FA4 后端的 1.33 倍。可直接参考其推荐掩码实现方式，但实验没有测量推荐精度增益。

original_abstract.text: Dynamic vocabularies built on-the-fly via Lempel-Ziv-Welch (LZW) compression let a language model represent the same text in fewer tokens, but prior work shows that this efficiency comes at a cost to reasoning and perplexity. We show that this quality gap is not a fundamental price of compression but can be substantially closed through targeted improvements to the compression layer and LZW codec, without modifying the underlying pretrained language model. Our analysis reveals four key issues: (1) LZW's compression algorithm creates an implicit conflict between the input embedding and the output embedding, a tension that a single shared embedding cannot resolve; (2) naively applying RoPE to LZW-compressed sequences ignores that merged tokens can span multiple tokens; (3) merging certain tokens (notably digits) disproportionately hurts downstream accuracy; and (4) dynamic vocabularies introduce an inherent segmentation ambiguity that confounds standard evaluation. We address these through decoupled input/output dynamic embedding layer, size-aware RoPE positioning, and a modified LZW codec supporting selective merges and multi-view segmentations. Across four models, our recipe improves perplexity on every corpus we evaluated as well as mathematical reasoning accuracy, closing roughly half the quality gap between zip2zip and the uncompressed baseline at a similar compression ratio on general text. This represents a significant step toward lossless adaptive-vocabulary compression for language models.
original_abstract.source_title: zip2zip++: Towards Inference-Time Token Compression with Minimal Quality Loss

en.text: zip2zip++ improves dynamic LZW token compression with separate input/output embeddings, size-aware RoPE and selective merges plus alternative segmentations. Across four models it improves tested-corpus perplexity and mathematical reasoning, closing roughly half the quality gap to uncompressed models at similar general-text compression ratios. It remains lossy in quality; transfer to compressed recommendation token streams is untested.

zh.text: 动态合并词元可以缩短序列，但会影响位置表示及输入输出嵌入。zip2zip++分别调整这些环节，并限制不利合并、处理多种切分方式。在四个模型中改善了所测语料困惑度与数学推理，在相近通用文本压缩率下弥合约一半质量差距，仍未完全恢复未压缩模型表现；推荐词元序列上的效果尚待验证。

original_abstract.text: Attention Residuals (AttnRes) enables content-dependent retrieval over network depth, which can be viewed as single-stream softmax attention along the depth axis. Inspired by the success of multi-head attention along the sequence axis, we introduce Multi-Stream Attention Residuals (MSAR), an extension of AttnRes that generalizes this mechanism to multi-head depth attention, yielding substantial performance gains with minimal additional overhead. MSAR draws stream diversity from sequence context through multi-scale causal convolutions, allowing different heads to retrieve historical representations through distinct contextual views while preserving the integrity of the hidden representation. The retrieved streams are combined through lightweight adaptive mixing to generate the single-stream layer input. By retaining single-stream sources and expanding them on demand, MSAR supports multi-stream computation without requiring persistent multi-stream storage or communication. Across all 12 downstream benchmarks at the 18B and 28B MoE scales, MSAR consistently outperforms prior residual variants, including standard residual connections, manifold-constrained Hyper-Connections (mHC), and AttnRes. Scaling-law experiments yield an iso-loss compute speedup of $1.58\times$ over the standard residual baseline, compared with $1.35\times$ for AttnRes and $1.30\times$ for mHC. These results make MSAR a promising residual architecture for large-scale pre-training.
original_abstract.source_title: Multi-Stream Attention Residuals

en.text: MSAR extends Attention Residuals to multiple depth-attention streams, deriving contextual views with multi-scale causal convolutions and mixing their retrieved representations. It retains single-stream stored sources and expands them on demand. In 18B and 28B MoE pretraining, it improves all 12 reported downstream benchmarks over the compared residual variants; scaling fits imply 1.58× iso-loss compute efficiency versus standard residuals. This is a depth-scaling design reference, not measured CTR improvement or 1.58× wall-clock training acceleration.

zh.text: MSAR 将 Attention Residuals 扩展为多路深度注意力，用多尺度因果卷积形成不同上下文视角，再融合检索结果；历史来源仍以单路保存，按需展开。18B、28B MoE 预训练中，12 项下游基准均优于所比较的残差方案；拟合结果给出相对标准残差 1.58 倍的同损失计算效率。可供深度扩展设计参考，不能解释为 CTR 收益或实际训练时间加速 1.58 倍。

original_abstract.text: Linearizing softmax attention offers a route to efficient Transformer inference, but preserving pretrained attention remains challenging. We identify an important source of approximation error overlooked by standard linearization methods: a small number of outlier dimensions contribute disproportionately to query-key dot products and account for a large fraction of the approximation error. Motivated by this heterogeneity, we propose Outlier-Aware Attention Linearization (OAL), a dimension-aware method for constructing quadratic attention approximations. Starting from a second-order Taylor approximation, we introduce a Hadamard-product formulation that makes individual query-key contributions explicit. This formulation relaxes globally shared coefficients to support dimension-specific linear terms and cross-dimensional quadratic interactions while preserving separable evaluation. To retain this flexibility with fewer parameters, OAL groups dimensions with similar contribution scales to share coefficients, while allowing distinct treatment of the few outliers. The resulting positive quadratic kernel is calibrated against pretrained attention outputs and admits linear-time evaluation with respect to sequence length for fixed head dimensions. On Qwen2.5-0.5B, OAL reduces frozen-attention output relative MSE by approximately 8.9% compared with DiJiang. Replacing middle-layer attention modules and jointly fine-tuning the kernel coefficients with LoRA further lowers WikiText-103 perplexity from 31.71 to 27.50 compared with a learned global quadratic, while improving accuracy on PIQA, HellaSwag, and ARC-E. These results demonstrate the value of outlier-aware dimension grouping for both attention approximation and pretrained-model conversion. The code is available at https://github.com/wuqianyue09/OAL
original_abstract.source_title: Not All Dimensions Are Equal: Outlier-Aware Attention Linearization with Grouped Quadratic Kernels

en.text: OAL approximates pretrained attention with a positive quadratic kernel whose coefficients distinguish outlier dimensions and share parameters within contribution-scale groups. On Qwen2.5-0.5B, frozen-attention relative MSE falls about 8.9% versus DiJiang; matched middle-layer conversion with LoRA lowers WikiText-103 perplexity from 31.71 to 27.50 versus a learned global quadratic, while retaining a gap to adapted softmax. Linear sequence-length complexity assumes fixed head dimensions; recommendation and production speed gains remain untested.

zh.text: OAL 用正值二次核近似预训练注意力，单独处理异常维度，并让贡献尺度相近的维度共享系数。在 Qwen2.5-0.5B 上，冻结注意力的相对均方误差比 DiJiang 低约 8.9%；配合 LoRA 转换中间层后，WikiText-103 困惑度相对可学习全局二次核从 31.71 降到 27.50，但仍落后于适配后的 softmax。序列长度线性复杂度以头维度固定为条件，推荐与生产加速尚未验证。

original_abstract.text: Long-context serving runs out of KV memory before the hardware reaches its useful throughput. HiSparse stores history in host memory and fetches only the selected entries, but it uses one cache budget at every load and does not handle draft-model speculative decoding such as DSpark and DFlash2. We present Adaptive DHiSparse, which supports speculative decoding over hierarchical sparse KV and adapts residency to load. It protects the required working set, retains additional history while GPU memory is spare, and recovers the rest through exact fused retrieval. DSpark and DFlash2 keep their proposal and acceptance rules: queries share missing-row retrieval, draft KV uses a window-bounded ring, and verification staging is reused across layer groups. At 100K context and concurrency 128, GLM-5.3 with DFlash2 delivers 793 output tokens/s per decode GPU, 1.45$\times$ HiSparse and 1.27$\times$ non-speculative adaptive serving. Held to the same latency bounds as HiSparse, it sustains up to 4$\times$ the concurrency and 2.3 to 3.7$\times$ the output, depending on the per-token bound. On DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash at 500K context and concurrency 512, Adaptive DHiSparse with DSpark delivers 1.85$\times$ the output of resident serving with DSpark. In a load step, optional residency reduces host fetches from 14.2% to 1.4% of selected rows at low load and releases memory under pressure.
original_abstract.source_title: Adaptive DHiSparse: Speculative Decoding over a Load-Adaptive KV Hierarchy

en.text: Adaptive DHiSparse combines load-adaptive GPU/host KV residency with draft-model speculative decoding, sharing missing-row retrieval while preserving the draft and acceptance rules. On B300 hardware with GLM-5.3, 100K context, and concurrency 128, it reports 793 output tokens/s per decode GPU, 1.45× HiSparse; prepared prefixes are reused in these workloads. It offers a memory-admission and serving co-design reference for long histories, while transfer to ranking workloads and broader request distributions remains unverified.

zh.text: Adaptive DHiSparse 结合随负载调整的 GPU/主机 KV 驻留和草稿模型推测解码，共享缺失行检索，同时保留草稿与接受规则。在 B300、GLM-5.3、100K 上下文和并发 128 的设置下，每张解码 GPU 输出 793 token/s，为 HiSparse 的 1.45 倍；这些负载复用了预备前缀。可借鉴其内存准入与服务协同设计，排序负载及更广请求分布上的迁移仍未验证。

original_abstract.text: Efficient attention mechanisms, such as linear and sliding window attention, aim to reduce the computational complexity of Transformers from quadratic to linear. However, their degraded in-context recall often necessitates interleaving full attention layers, leaving the quadratic bottleneck unresolved in long-context processing. To address this, we introduce Orthros attention, which shifts the efficiency paradigm from structural allocation to phase-aware decoupling. As a unified module, it dynamically switches its computation pattern across different phases of sequence processing, enabling linear complexity prefilling and full attention decoding. Our design grants Orthros attention a lower asymptotic complexity compared to vanilla Transformers in prevalent long-context scenarios characterized by heavy prefilling and light decoding. Beyond theoretical formulation and complexity analysis, extensive empirical evaluations demonstrate Orthros's superiority across multiple dimensions. First, we validate its fundamental language modeling capabilities, demonstrating scalability across varying model sizes and strong competitiveness in comprehensive architectural comparisons. Second, Orthros exhibits exceptional conversion feasibility via a data-efficient Transformer-to-Orthros conversion, yielding performance that even surpasses the original Transformer. Finally, Orthros achieves a $21.9\times$ prefilling speedup over Transformers with end-to-end inference gains, while preserving long-context capabilities, as demonstrated by near-perfect 128K needle-in-a-haystack results and Transformer-level performance on real-world in-context recall tasks. Overall, these advantages in high performance, flexibility, and efficiency position Orthros as a promising candidate to succeed the Transformer in industrial applications.
original_abstract.source_title: Orthros: Phase-Aware Heterogeneous Attention for Efficient Transformers

en.text: Orthros changes attention computation by phase: linear-complexity prefill is paired with full-attention decoding. Language-model pretraining, conversion, and recall evaluations support the design for long prompts with comparatively short generation; the reported 21.9× prefill speedup occurs at one-million-token length and is not a universal end-to-end gain. Its phase-aware design may inform long-history processing, but CTR transfer has not been demonstrated.

zh.text: Orthros 按处理阶段改变注意力计算：预填充采用线性复杂度路径，解码保留完整注意力。语言模型预训练、转换与召回测试支持其用于长输入、较短生成的场景；21.9 倍预填充加速对应百万 token 长度，不能当作普遍端到端收益。阶段分工可供长历史处理参考，尚未验证 CTR 迁移。

original_abstract.text: Low-bit inference on accelerators with native 4-bit support requires quantizing both weights and activations to realize the full throughput gains these formats provide. While post-training weight quantization has been extensively studied, activation quantization remains considerably more challenging and typically requires calibration data. In this work, we introduce DUALQUANT, a dual-scale, calibration-free post-training quantization framework that directly minimizes the weight-reconstruction Mean Squared Error (MSE) and, as an immediate by-product, yields per-channel activation rescalings prior to activation quantization. Our key observation is that the scaling factors obtained by minimizing weight-reconstruction error provide effective activation rescalings, enabling competitive activation quantization without calibration data. We formulate DUALQUANT as a non-differentiable weight-reconstruction problem and develop an efficient solver based on variable splitting and block coordinate descent, where each subproblem admits a closed-form update. DUALQUANT provides a unified algorithm supporting a wide range of formats, including the full MX family and NVFP4. To our knowledge, DUALQUANT is the first dual-scaling method to formally support MX and NV block formats. Across Llama and Qwen models evaluated on WikiText-2, C4, and zero-shot downstream tasks, DUALQUANT matches or exceeds the accuracy of calibration-based SmoothQuant across most models and formats, and substantially outperforms calibration-free baselines, with large gains for MX and NV block formats. We validate these gains with a real packed W4A4 inference path for Llama-3.1-8B on an RTX 4090. The resulting implementation closely matches the accuracy of fake quantization while delivering up to 2.61x memory reduction and up to 2.46x throughput speedup over BF16.
original_abstract.source_title: DualQuant: Dual-scale Calibration-free Weight-and-Activation Quantization for LLMs

en.text: DualQuant jointly optimizes weight-reconstruction scales and obtains per-channel activation rescaling without calibration data, supporting MX and NVFP4 formats. Llama and Qwen evaluations compare accuracy across formats; a packed W4A4 path for Llama-3.1-8B on RTX 4090 reports up to 2.61x memory reduction and 2.46x throughput speedup over BF16. It suggests a calibration-free compression route for scalable models, but recommendation transfer and hardware-specific efficiency need separate measurement.

zh.text: DualQuant 联合优化权重重建的缩放因子，并从中得到逐通道激活缩放，无需校准数据，支持MX与NVFP4等格式。除Llama/Qwen精度评测外，Llama-3.1-8B在RTX4090上的实际W4A4实现报告，相对BF16，内存压缩比最高2.61倍、吞吐最高提升至2.46倍。可借鉴其免校准压缩思路，但推荐迁移与不同硬件上的效率仍需单独测量。

original_abstract.text: State-space models (SSMs) maintain a fixed-size recurrent state, but reading and writing it at every decoding step can bottleneck hybrid models. This eager state management causes large state I/O with low arithmetic intensity, leaves speculative decoding no cheap rollback, and feeds state quantization error into subsequent recurrent updates. We introduce ReplaySSM, which unrolls the recurrence to represent the state as a checkpoint and a buffer of recent SSM inputs. This separates output computation from checkpoint updates. By updating the checkpoint periodically, ReplaySSM avoids state writes on most steps and roughly halves the dominant state memory traffic. Keeping recent inputs also makes speculative rollback a buffer-pointer operation and enables output-only verification without materializing intermediate states. The same separation allows a low-precision checkpoint to serve output computation on most steps while a higher-precision checkpoint serves recurrent updates, so rounding error in the low-precision copy never enters later updates. We implement ReplaySSM in vLLM for Mamba-2 and Gated DeltaNet. At serving batch size 256, it accelerates standard decoding by $1.20$--$1.47\times$ over a tuned vLLM baseline across four hybrid models, and delivers about $1.8\times$ the throughput of vLLM's speculative decoding on the two 120B-class models. Separate state precisions also reduce output KL divergence and downstream accuracy losses compared with a shared low-precision checkpoint.
original_abstract.source_title: ReplaySSM: Cache SSM Inputs, Not State

en.text: ReplaySSM represents recurrent state with a checkpoint plus recent inputs, deferring checkpoint writes and supporting cheap speculative rollback. Separate state precisions prevent low-precision output reads from feeding rounding error back into recurrent updates. At batch size 256, four hybrid language models obtain 1.20–1.47x standard-decoding speedups over tuned vLLM. It informs memory-traffic optimization for recurrent sequence models; batch-one results are below parity, and recommendation benefits remain untested.

zh.text: ReplaySSM 用检查点与近期输入共同表示递归状态，延迟状态写入，并让投机解码能低成本回退；输出读取与状态更新使用不同精度，避免低精度误差反馈到后续递归。在batch=256下，四种混合语言模型相对调优后的vLLM实现1.20–1.47倍常规解码加速。可借鉴其递归序列模型访存优化；batch=1时未提速，推荐收益尚未验证。

original_abstract.text: Production recommender systems have feature-lifecycle asymmetry: adding new features must produce gains on some metric, while feature removal must not regress any metric. In practice, feature deprecation is hard to prioritize as a feature can fail to be removed if it interacts with other features, its importance changes daily, it cannot be evaluated before production models change or data drift occurs, it is in contention for A/B test space with other launches, it causes regressions in an online A/B test, or it is consumed by multiple models that need to coordinate its deprecation. We present FORTE, a model-agnostic production framework for discovering, validating, and removing features. Its efficient perturbation implementation allows daily feature evaluation. To account for interactions, it evaluates candidate feature sets constructed from all the low-rank features through grouped ablation and its offline results are sufficiently predictive of online A/B tests to allow deprecations to proceed to online testing with confidence. Lineage tracing identifies all downstream consumer models to realize the full savings of removing a feature from the training set. We validate FORTE over 2 large-scale recommender systems and find that it identifies deprecable feature sets which do not cause online regressions, while the impact on efficiency depends on model characteristics. On a search-relevance model, FORTE resulted in 3 nested candidate sets of 32, 48, and 59 features. Online guardrails rejected the largest treatment. The 48-feature set was selected for deprecation, removing 43.3% of the model's features. On a large ranking model, FORTE identified 8 candidates for removal. Retraining and A/B testing confirmed no regression. Its launch reduced the trainable parameters by 29.9%, improved serving throughput by 19.8-25.5%, and reduced annual training costs by hundreds of thousands of dollars.
original_abstract.source_title: FORTE: A Production Framework for Feature Evaluation and Deprecation in Industrial Recommender Systems

en.text: FORTE screens feature-removal candidates with repeated perturbation measurements, grouped ablations, retraining, online guardrails, and downstream lineage tracing. In two Pinterest recommender systems, the largest search-model removal set failed online guardrails, while removing eight features from a separate ranking model reduced trainable parameters by 29.9% and raised serving throughput by 19.8–25.5%. It offers a production process for reclaiming ranking-system capacity, not a guarantee that low individual importance makes a feature safe to remove.

zh.text: FORTE 通过持续扰动评估、成组消融、重训练、线上护栏和下游依赖追踪，筛选可删除特征。在 Pinterest 两套推荐系统中，搜索模型的最大删除方案未通过线上护栏；另一排序模型删除 8 个特征后，可训练参数减少 29.9%，服务吞吐提高 19.8–25.5%。可借鉴这套释放排序系统容量的流程，不能仅凭单特征重要性低就认定可安全删除。

original_abstract.text: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models have emerged as an effective paradigm for scaling large language models, yet their massive parameter footprint poses severe memory challenges for deployment. Existing compression methods typically treat expert pruning and merging as disjoint operations and rely on greedy heuristics, often leading to irreversible information loss or representational pollution. In this paper, we propose PRIME, a unified optimization framework for MoE compression via adaptive PRunIng and MErging. PRIME casts the discrete prune-merge assignment step as a global Integer Linear Programming over a frequency-weighted surrogate objective, jointly selecting pruning and merging decisions while accounting for expert usage. We motivate the frequency-aware objective through an error-bound analysis under fixed representative assignments, and show that the formulation favors high-frequency experts as centroids, promoting routing stability. Extensive experiments on Qwen3-30B-A3B and Qwen3.5-122B-A10B demonstrate that PRIME achieves strong accuracy retention across knowledge, coding, math, and long-context tasks, while serving benchmarks of merged models quantify the memory and throughput benefits of expert compression in vLLM.
original_abstract.source_title: PRIME: Frequency-Aware Unified Pruning and Merging for MoE Compression

en.text: PRIME jointly chooses expert pruning and merging through a global integer-linear optimization with a frequency-weighted surrogate objective. Experiments on Qwen3-30B-A3B and Qwen3.5-122B-A10B assess retained quality across knowledge, coding, mathematics and long-context tasks, with vLLM serving measurements of memory and throughput. The work offers a coordinated expert-compression design; gains for recommendation MoE models remain untested.

zh.text: MoE压缩若把删除专家与合并专家分开处理，容易损失信息。PRIME将两种选择放进同一个整数线性优化问题，并按专家使用频率加权。在两种Qwen模型上评估知识、代码、数学和长上下文质量，也用vLLM测量内存与吞吐收益。该方法可供推荐MoE的专家压缩参考，但尚无直接迁移验证。

original_abstract.text: Sparse attention visits few keys, yet finding them can still require scoring every key with every indexer head. We introduce DoSA (Dots Sparse Attention), a lossless method for making this computation conditional while preserving exact token selection. Its central observation is that Top-K selection requires sufficient evidence to reject a candidate, not necessarily its full score. A seed set supplies a lower bound on the winning threshold. Nonnegative head projections and joint residual bounds upper-bound positive contributions, while activation-informed aggregation bounds the magnitude subtracted by negative heads. The certificate directs full scoring toward candidates that remain eligible; exact-score filtering further reduces writeback and selection work. We establish the certificate and its exact-selection conditions, and analyze how geometry and selection margins govern its effectiveness. Our GPU implementation accelerates the complete Indexer by up to 2.74 times over SGLang and 1.69 times over LiteTopK across English, Chinese, and code workloads. End-to-end evaluation on GLM-5.2 and DeepSeek-V3.2 achieves up to 1.94 times and 1.50 times time-to-first-token speedups over the two baselines, respectively.
original_abstract.source_title: DoSA: Dots Sparse Attention

en.text: DoSA avoids fully scoring sparse-attention indexer candidates that provable bounds already rule out, preserving exact token selection under its stated conditions. The GPU implementation speeds up the full indexer by up to 2.74x over SGLang and 1.69x over LiteTopK. End-to-end tests on GLM-5.2 and DeepSeek-V3.2 report time-to-first-token speedups up to 1.94x and 1.50x against those baselines. Transfer to recommendation indexing remains untested.

zh.text: 稀疏注意力只读取少量词元，但筛选这些词元仍可能遍历全部历史。DoSA利用得分上下界提前排除不可能进入Top-K的候选，在给定条件下保持精确选择。作者报告完整索引器相对SGLang和LiteTopK最高加速2.74倍、1.69倍，所测模型首词元延迟最高改善1.94倍、1.50倍；推荐索引场景尚待验证。

original_abstract.text:
Late-interaction (multi-vector) models represent documents using a set of token-level vectors, providing a middle ground between cross-encoders and dense encoders in terms of quality and cost of embedding. However, compared to the latter, the indices are costly to store and score. Pooling and pruning based compression techniques are deployed widely but deteriorate in quality noticeably with aggressive compression. We investigate whether a lightweight change to the scoring function can recover retrieval quality after document-vector compression. For each combination of encoder, compressor, and vector budget, we learn a global linear correction by distilling the uncompressed model's score distributions over candidate documents. The encoder and compressor remain frozen, and the correction can be applied to each query at search time or once, offline, to the stored vectors.
  We evaluate the method with ColBERTv2 and Jina v4 on MS MARCO and BEIR, and with ColPali2 on the ViDoRe v3 visual document retrieval benchmark. Experiments cover four training-free compression methods, multiple vector budgets, in-domain adaptation, and transfer from MS MARCO to BEIR. In the in-domain setting, the correction improves over baseline compression in 154 of 160 BEIR settings, while transfer from MS MARCO is more variable across models and datasets. We also find that matrices trained with synthetic queries can improve over baseline compression on ViDoRe v3. These results show that a small learned correction can recover some of the quality lost to compression without retraining the encoder or recompressing the documents.
original_abstract.source_title: Simple Linear Corrections for Compression in Late Interaction

en.text: A lightweight linear correction distills uncompressed late-interaction retrieval scores after document-vector compression, leaving the encoder and compressor frozen. Across ColBERTv2, Jina v4 and ColPali2 experiments, it improves 154 of 160 in-domain BEIR settings; transfer from MS MARCO is more variable. The correction can be applied at query time or to stored vectors offline, recovering some quality without retraining encoders or recompressing documents.

zh.text: 多向量检索压缩文档表示后，相关性评分容易失真。该研究固定编码器和压缩器，仅蒸馏未压缩模型的得分，学习一个线性修正；可在查询时应用，也可离线作用于存储向量。在域内BEIR测试中，160组设置有154组改善，但从MS MARCO迁移的效果更不稳定。它提供了无需重训编码器或重新压缩文档的补偿方法。

original_abstract.text: Softmax attention in Transformers suffers from quadratic complexity in sequence length, making it impractical for long-context applications. Linear attention alleviates this issue by replacing the exponential kernel with alternative functions that enable linear-time computation. Among existing linear attention approaches, recent studies have shown that polynomial kernels are particularly effective, as they exhibit sparse and spiky behavior similar to softmax attention, which emphasizes large dot products while suppressing irrelevant interactions. However, the exact computation of high-degree polynomial kernels is infeasible for high-dimensional representations. As a result, prior work relies on approximate polynomial kernels. This introduces a non-negligible approximation error. In this paper, we show that, from the perspective of polynomial kernel approximation, existing linear attention methods are still suboptimal. We propose \textbf{L}earnable \textbf{Lo}w-Rank \textbf{P}olynomial \textbf{S}ketch (LLoPS), a principled and flexible framework for approximating polynomial kernels with linear attention. Our method learns a low-rank polynomial sketch that provably achieves a strictly smaller approximation error than existing approaches. Experiment results show that LLoPS achieves the highest performance across extensive benchmarks, comparing with various linear attention baselines.
original_abstract.source_title: Learnable Low-Rank Polynomial Sketch for Effective Linear Attention

en.text: LLoPS learns low-rank polynomial feature sketches for linear attention, aiming to reduce approximation error relative to existing polynomial-kernel constructions. It reports strong results against tested linear-attention baselines across language and long-range benchmarks. The language study adapts BASED checkpoints with matched continued training for the BASED comparator. The theoretical approximation result is not a guarantee of better task accuracy; possible long-history ranking use remains untested.

zh.text: LLoPS 学习低秩多项式特征映射，以降低既有多项式核线性注意力的近似误差，并在语言与长距离基准上报告对所测线性注意力基线的较强表现。语言实验由 BASED 检查点继续训练，同时对 BASED 对照执行匹配的继续训练。核近似理论不等于所有任务准确率必然提高；对长历史排序的用途仍待验证。

original_abstract.text: Scaling deep learning models efficiently requires predictable performance transfer across compute regimes. Establishing reliable hyperparameter transfer allows optimal training dynamics and structural choices to be discovered on low-cost proxy models, avoiding catastrophic failures during massive-scale training. Existing depth-transfer analyses are architecture-specific and heuristic: hyperparameter transfer is only justified through toy blocks, and both rely on infinite-depth dynamics, a specific initialization, and feature-learning criteria. Building on $L$-smoothness framework of Xu et al. (2026), we understand hyperparameter transfer as how do the Lipschitz and $L$-smoothness constants of the loss scale with the depth $K$? We show that inverse-depth residual branch scaling $α=Θ(1/K)$ is sufficient to make both constants depth-independent at fixed width, uniformly over the bounded parameter domain and for arbitrary $p\to q$ geometries. Because the bounds depend on each residual branch only through its Lipschitz and smoothness constants, the argument applies to general residual networks (including branches of block depth $\geq 2$ such as transformer and ResNet blocks) without assumptions on initialization or correlations between layer weights. Since the smoothness constant controls the curvature penalty in the descent inequality, our bounds motivate a learning-rate scale without an additional depth-dependent curvature correction for updates bounded in the prescribed norm. This provides a geometric explanation of inverse-depth residual scaling and its application to the operator-norm geometries associated with AdamW, Muon, and MOGA. Learning-rate sweeps on GPT-2 (depths 2--128) and CIFAR-100 ResNets (8--32 residual blocks) confirm that Muon and MOGA exhibit stable learning-rate transfer under these prescriptions, with a common optimal rate across a 64-fold increase in depth.
original_abstract.source_title: On the Depth Transfer of Neural Optimizers via L-Smoothness

en.text: The paper analyzes depth transfer through loss Lipschitz and smoothness constants, showing that inverse-depth residual scaling can keep these bounds depth-independent at fixed width under its assumptions. Learning-rate sweeps on GPT-2 and CIFAR-100 ResNets support stable Muon/MOGA transfer, including a common optimal rate across a 64-fold depth increase. This informs deep-model scaling recipes; recommender applicability remains untested.

zh.text: 小模型上找到的学习率能否用于更深模型，是扩大训练规模的关键问题。该文从损失函数的平滑性分析残差分支按深度倒数缩放的作用，并在GPT-2和CIFAR-100 ResNet上检验。Muon和MOGA在所测条件下表现出稳定的学习率迁移，包括深度增大64倍时共享最优学习率；对推荐模型的适用性仍待验证。

original_abstract.text: Training large-scale recommender systems on dynamic industrial platforms, such as Short-Form Video (SFV) services with billions of daily interactions, faces critical stability challenges. Rapid distribution shifts in user data and increasing model complexity frequently trigger a divergence cascade, typically initiating with gradient explosion, propagating to weight explosion, and culminating in loss explosion. This G-W-L cascade severely impedes model convergence and performance. This paper provides a systematic analysis of this G-W-L cascade within an industrial SFV recommender context. We then propose and evaluate a structured mitigation framework where interventions are explicitly mapped to counteract specific stages of the cascade: gradient (G) control, weight/activation (W) stabilization, and loss (L) shaping. Our contribution provides a structured framework for understanding and tackling training divergence, offering practical insights for deploying robust, continuously updated recommenders in large-scale, non-stationary settings. We empirically validate the effectiveness of these strategies on a major industrial SFV recommendation system.
original_abstract.source_title: Understanding and Mitigating Training Instability in Large-Scale Recommender Systems: A Cascade Perspective

en.text: This study analyzes training divergence in an industrial short-video recommender as a coupled gradient–weight–loss cascade and groups interventions into gradient control, weight/activation stabilization, and loss shaping. Industrial experiments support combining these controls to stabilize continuously updated models under distribution shifts. The measurements do not establish the exact temporal cascade for every divergence event; the work offers a practical diagnostic framework for scaling rankers rather than a universal causal law.

zh.text: 论文把工业短视频推荐中的训练发散整理为梯度、权重与损失相互影响的过程，并将干预分成梯度控制、权重与激活稳定、损失调整三类。工业实验支持组合这些措施，以稳定分布变化下持续更新的模型。现有测量未逐次证明所有发散事件的先后因果链；它为排序模型扩容提供诊断框架，而非普适因果定律。

original_abstract.text: Frontier AI systems are increasingly natively multimodal, jointly pretrained on multiple modalities, such as text, vision, and audio. However, the scientific understanding of the multimodal data mixtures used to pretrain these systems --- how much of each modality to mix, and at what potential interference cost to the others --- is largely absent or gatekept. In this work, we derive data mixing scaling laws for three modalities: text, vision, and audio. Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) increasingly adopt Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architectures, as MoEs scale efficiently and partially limit cross-modal interference. We therefore use MoEs to conduct 268 experiments ranging from 457M to 8.3B parameters, on up to 150 billion tokens. Our work leads to multiple actionable insights into multimodal data mixing for training MLLMs. First, compute optima are modality-specific: audio modality is model-heavy, favoring scaling parameters over tokens, while text and vision require balanced scaling of model size and data. Second, repeating vision or audio data beyond 2x yields negligible benefits. Finally, cross-modal interactions are highly asymmetric: vision strongly interferes with audio, whereas audio's interference with learning text and vision is negligible. Overall, we provide a principled foundation for understanding the multimodal data mixtures needed to train frontier MLLMs.
original_abstract.source_title: Scaling Laws for Multimodal Data Mixtures

en.text: This multimodal scaling study fits data-mixture laws from 268 MoE experiments spanning 457M–8.3B parameters and up to 150B tokens. Compute-optimal allocation differs by modality: audio favors parameters more strongly, while text and vision favor balanced model/data growth. Repeating vision or audio data beyond twice offers negligible benefits, and cross-modal interference is asymmetric. These findings may guide multimodal recommendation budgeting, but that transfer is untested.

zh.text: 多模态训练需要决定模型规模、各模态数据量及混合比例。该研究开展268组MoE实验，覆盖457M至8.3B参数和最高150B词元，发现音频更偏向扩大参数，文本与视觉更需要模型和数据均衡增长；视觉或音频数据重复超过两遍收益很小，模态间干扰也不对称。这些规律可供多模态推荐预算研究参考，尚不能直接当作推荐系统结论。
